All mechanisms fit similarly well except M20 which is worse (likely overparameterized without discriminating data). The baseline experiment doesn't discriminate well - most models can fit a single time course. I need to vary conditions to expose mechanistic differences.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Key discriminative features to test:
1. **Catalyst order**: M2, M3 (dimerization) predict non-first-order catalyst dependence. M3 predicts higher-order (rate ∝ [cat]²ish at low cat, saturating). M13 (2cat→inactive) predicts more deactivation at high cat.
2. **Deactivation**: M9-M20 predict plateau below full conversion. Higher catalyst = more deactivation for M13, M18, M19 (bimolecular).

Best experiment: vary catalyst concentration significantly. High catalyst loading will:
- Amplify dimerization effects (M2, M3, M13)
- Amplify bimolecular deactivation (M13, M18, M19)
- Distinguish first-order vs. non-first-order catalyst dependence

Predictions at [cat]=0.1 (10× higher), [S]=1.0, [P]=0:
- M1, M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, M14, M15: reaction ~10× faster, reaches full conversion
- M9, M10, M11, M12, M14, M17: some deactivation, may not reach full conversion, but similar per-cat behavior
- M2 (dimer inactive form as resting state): slower per-cat at high loading
- M3 (dimer is active): faster than linear scaling
- M13, M18, M19: strong deactivation at high cat, low final conversion
- M16 (S+catS deactivation): similar to lower cat since bottleneck is different
</hypothesis>
